model_selection.summary: Native through CLI/session controls and subagent model frontmatter.

current_session.detail: The interactive session can change model and subagents can select their own model.

launcher.detail: The launcher can pass --model or managed model policy.

reasoning_effort.summary: Native effort controls exist, but accepted levels and mutability depend on model and client version.

current_session.detail: The session can set effort where the active model/version supports it.

launcher.detail: The launcher can pass --effort, subject to model/version support.

parallel_agents.summary: Background subagents run concurrently and a client setting caps their concurrency.

current_session.detail: The active session can start bounded background subagents.

agent_roles.summary: Custom subagents support role-specific model, tools, permissions, MCP, hooks, skills, effort, turns, and worktrees.

current_session.detail: Configured project roles can be selected during the session.

launcher.detail: The launcher or project files can supply custom role definitions.

context_budget.summary: PowerKit can scope reads and use subagent isolation, but no stable hard per-task context budget is documented.

current_session.detail: Repository scope and summaries are PowerKit-owned, not a provider hard limit.

launcher.detail: The launcher can isolate subagent context but cannot impose the canonical budget as a hard limit.

tool_restriction.summary: --tools controls availability; disallowedTools denies tools. allowedTools only preapproves and is not an allowlist.

current_session.detail: Tool availability is established for the session; role-specific subagents can be stricter.

launcher.detail: The launcher can set the available tools and explicit deny rules.

filesystem_scope.summary: Permission modes and OS sandboxing help, but built-in file tools are outside the Bash sandbox.

current_session.detail: Plan mode and tool denial can prevent edits; a running session cannot acquire a new OS boundary retroactively.

launcher.detail: Launch permissions, tool denial, and sandbox policy must be combined; no one control covers every file path.

network_restriction.summary: The sandbox uses proxy/domain policy, but built-in tools and unsandboxed fallback require separate handling.

current_session.detail: PowerKit must separately restrict Bash, WebFetch, MCP, Chrome, and other transports.

launcher.detail: A launcher can configure sandbox domains and failIfUnavailable, plus tool/MCP restrictions.

shell_restriction.summary: Bash availability and command-pattern permissions can be restricted explicitly.

current_session.detail: The active session keeps its tool inventory; stricter subagents can omit Bash.

launcher.detail: The launcher can omit Bash from --tools and add deny rules.

max_iterations.summary: Native for print mode, Agent SDK sessions, and subagents; not a hard cap for the main interactive session.

current_session.detail: Subagent maxTurns is native; the interactive root has no documented numeric turn cap.

launcher.detail: --max-turns applies to print mode, not every interactive workflow.

checkpoints.summary: Permission modes and blocking hooks gate concrete actions; semantic phase checkpoints remain workflow-owned.

current_session.detail: Blocking hooks and human prompts can gate supported events, not every semantic milestone.

launcher.detail: Launch permission modes and reviewed command hooks can establish action checkpoints.

execution_isolation.summary: Worktrees isolate Git edits and OS sandboxing limits processes, but neither is a full VM boundary.

current_session.detail: A running root session cannot be retroactively moved to a new worktree.

launcher.detail: --worktree and sandbox policy can isolate edits/processes without isolating all secrets or network.

runtime_browser.summary: Shell tests are native; Chrome integration is beta and shares signed-in browser state.

current_session.detail: Chrome is usable only when installed, enabled, and appropriate for the signed-in profile.

launcher.detail: The launcher can enable/disable Chrome; availability remains client/account dependent.

usage_telemetry.summary: Opt-in OpenTelemetry exposes metrics/events/traces; provider retention and operational telemetry are separate.

current_session.detail: Capture only metrics actually emitted by the configured client.

launcher.detail: A launcher can configure OTel, while service-side retention remains outside PowerKit control.

external_write_gating.summary: Permissions and hooks gate known tools, but external writes require tool-specific authorization.

current_session.detail: Known tool events can be blocked; task depth never authorizes the external action.

launcher.detail: Deny/ask rules and hooks can gate declared external-write tools.

mcp_restriction.summary: Strict MCP config and managed/server/tool allowlists exist; identity matching must include URL or command.

current_session.detail: The active session uses its loaded MCP set; PowerKit can avoid exposed tools but not unload them.

launcher.detail: --strict-mcp-config and managed identity/tool policies can restrict MCP at launch.

translations.note: Aliases are adapter data and remain subject to managed availableModels policy.
NARROW_SCOPED_WRITE also requires explicit tool and sandbox policy.
With no explicit MCP config, strict mode ignores discovered MCP servers.
A worktree is not a security sandbox.

cli.label: local CLI
cli.validation_detail: A broker-owned stdin invocation on Claude Code 2.1.123 passed haiku, low effort, one-agent cap, plan permission mode, a read-only tool allowlist plus Bash denial, strict empty MCP configuration, no settings sources/browser/slash commands, local non-persistence, and four maximum turns, then returned the expected response on 2026-08-17; this validates that combination, not every control row.
